requests.label: chromatin_stripe
requests.definition: A DNA region in which a single anchor point contacts a continuous span of sequence to one side, producing a linear band of elevated contact frequency in a chromosome conformation capture contact map.
requests.rationale: SO already covers the rest of the standard Hi-C feature vocabulary: TAD, TAD boundary, DNA loop and DNA loop anchor all have terms. Stripes (also called flames or architectural stripes) are the one common Hi-C feature class with no SO term, so stripe calls have nowhere to point.

requests.label: chromatin_compartment
requests.definition: A megabase-scale DNA region assigned to one of the two mutually segregated spatial compartments (A or B) resolved from a chromosome conformation capture contact map.
requests.rationale: A/B compartments are the coarsest standard feature derived from Hi-C data. SO covers the finer levels of the same hierarchy (TADs, loops) but has no term at the compartment level.

requests.label: chromatin_subcompartment
requests.definition: A DNA region assigned to one of the finer spatial subdivisions of a chromatin compartment, such as A1, A2, B1, B2, B3 or B4.
requests.rationale: Subcompartments (A1, A2, B1-B4) are routinely reported alongside compartment calls and are strictly finer than them, so they need the proposed chromatin_compartment term as a parent.

requests.label: TF_footprint
requests.definition: A short DNA region within an accessible chromatin region that is protected from nuclease cleavage by a bound transcription factor.
requests.rationale: SO has DNaseI_hypersensitive_site and accessible_DNA_region, which describe the surrounding open region, but nothing for the protected sub-region that marks actual factor occupancy. That sub-region is what footprinting assays report, and it is a narrower thing than either the accessible region or the generic binding site.

requests.label: CpG_site
requests.definition: A cytosine immediately followed by a guanine on the same strand of a DNA molecule.

additionalTerms.label: CHG_site
additionalTerms.definition: A cytosine followed by any base other than guanine and then a guanine, on the same strand of a DNA molecule.

additionalTerms.label: CHH_site
additionalTerms.definition: A cytosine followed by two bases, neither of which is guanine, on the same strand of a DNA molecule.

requests.rationale: SO has CpG_island but no term for the dinucleotide itself, which is the unit every methylation track actually reports (one row per site). The only existing CpG mention is the variant term C_to_T_transition_at_pCpG_site, which is not a feature class. CHG and CHH siblings are needed for plant and non-CG methylation data.

requests.label: two_prime_O_methylated_nucleotide
requests.definition: A nucleotide carrying a methyl group on the 2'-hydroxyl of its ribose, irrespective of base identity.
requests.rationale: SO has six base-specific 2'-O-methyl terms, but each one hangs off its own base-specific parent (modified_adenosine, modified_cytidine and so on), so there is no grouping class that collects them. Generic Nm data, which does not resolve the underlying base, therefore has nowhere to point.

requests.label: nucleosome
requests.definition: A DNA region of approximately 147 base pairs wrapped around a histone octamer.
requests.rationale: Verified absent from SO, which is surprising given how central nucleosome positioning is to chromatin data. The word appears only inside the definitions of other terms, never as a term label or synonym. GO covers the nucleosome as a cellular component but not as a region of sequence.
requests.note: Lower confidence than the rest. The motivating ONGA term, "valleys", is a weak signal for nucleosome positioning rather than a direct request for the concept, so the evidence from ONGA alone is thin even though the gap in SO is real.

requests.label: replication_timing_domain
requests.definition: A DNA region that replicates as a coordinated unit at a characteristic time during S phase.
requests.rationale: SO has origin_of_replication but nothing for the early- and late-replicating domains that replication timing assays segment the genome into.
requests.note: Medium confidence because both motivating ONGA terms name a profile or a signal rather than a segmented domain, so they sit close to the measurement-versus-feature line that sends other terms to EDAM. The domain itself is still a genuine sequence region and belongs in SO.

requests.label: loop
requests.requestedChange: Disambiguate the label. Either rename the term to something that names its RNA secondary-structure context, or add an explicit comment stating that chromatin and DNA loops are SO:0002307 DNA_loop and not this term.
requests.rationale: SO:0002254 is defined as the loop portion of a stem-loop and sits under stem_loop_region, an RNA secondary-structure branch. Its bare label "loop" collides head-on with chromatin loops, which are SO:0002307 DNA_loop under chromosome_part. Any name-based or string-similarity mapping tool matches chromatin loop data to SO:0002254 and gets the meaning exactly backwards.
requests.note: No single ONGA term motivates this. It surfaced from the mapping process itself, when name-based matching of ONGA chromatin loop concepts landed on the RNA term.

requests.label: sequence_adapter
requests.definition: A short synthetic oligonucleotide ligated to the ends of a nucleic acid fragment during sequencing library preparation, providing the sequences required for platform binding, amplification and priming.
requests.rationale: SO covers the rest of the library-preparation reagent vocabulary -- primer, oligo, synthetic_oligo and the multiplexing index -- but has no term for the adapter itself. Verified absent from so.obo: neither "adapter" nor "adaptor" appears as a term name or as a synonym. Adapter sequences are one of the most routinely reported items in a sequencing run, and with no SO term the ONGA DataType `sequence adapters` has nowhere to point: it currently carries only a skos:relatedMatch to SO:0000150 read, which is wrong (an adapter is not a read) and is recorded as such rather than as an element type.
requests.note: Parent chosen as SO:0000696 oligo (under SO:0000695 reagent), the branch that already holds primer and synthetic_oligo, rather than the generic SO:0000110 sequence_feature. An adapter is a reagent sequence, not a feature of the genome being sequenced.

rejections.reason: These name a property of the biological sample, not a class of sequence feature. ONGA already ejects sample and assay axes out of its content scope to the ontology that owns them, and cell type is exactly that kind of axis. It belongs to CL, and it should not be pushed into SO.
rejections.precedent: mappings/scope_delegations.tsv, where anatomy qualifiers were ejected from ONGA content terms to UBERON. Cell type is the same move to CL.

rejections.reason: This is a relation between two features -- a regulatory element and the gene it acts on -- not a class of region. SO models what a stretch of sequence IS; a binary relation between two such stretches is what RO is for. Adding it to SO as a class would misrepresent its arity.

These are measurements, scores, reports and derived data products rather than classes of sequence feature. SO answers "what is this region"; each of these answers "what was measured or computed about some region", which is EDAM's domain. They are mapped through the EDAM mapping set instead of being sent to SO.

ongaTerms.term: transposable element TF ancestral origin percent by motif
transposable element TF ancestral origin percent by subfamily

rejections.reason: SO models INDIVIDUAL sequence features; each ONGA term below names a SET of them, which is ONGA's own scope. A set of enhancers is not an enhancer, so asking SO to mint a class for the set would push ONGA's vocabulary into SO and would assert the level shift the whole set/element rule exists to prevent. The correct treatment is the one already applied: the ONGA term stays in ONGA and points at the SO element type via onga:has_element_type in mappings/so.sssom.tsv. This rejection is standing policy, not a one-off: it applies to every future case where an ONGA set term is considered for an SO request. See the ADR "ONGA terms denote sets; SO terms denote elements".
rejections.precedent: mappings/so.sssom.tsv, where all 74 membership rows use onga:has_element_type instead of a SKOS match, and the only two SKOS matches left against SO are SO:0001505 reference_genome and SO:0001506 variant_genome -- SO classes that are THEMSELVES set-denoting ("A collection of sequences ..."), where no level shift occurs.
